name: Roland JUPITER-50
description: Roland JUPITER-50 synthesizer: the temporary registration (common, the UPPER, SOLO and PERC/LOWER parts, SOLO's and PERC/LOWER's sub part and tone modify, sixteen external parts), the UPPER live set (common, MFX structure, four MFX, reverb, and four layers each with tone offset, tone modify and tone blender), UPPER's four layer tones (SuperNATURAL Synth: common and three partials), and the setup and system blocks, from the MIDI Implementation.

sources.title: JUPITER-50 MIDI Implementation (version 1.00, April 30, 2012)
sources.notes: Parameter Address Map read by tools/profiles/roland/parse-address-map.mjs from JUPITER-50_MIDI_Imple_e01.pdf (sha256 5bd59c28335f68c2ea7680525ba250b8c6a3ef064d94bc7b13e60f18832a89e3). Model ID 00 00 63, DT1 = 12, RQ1 = 11, Roland checksum. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/roland/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/roland/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is the manual's, at the manual's address, with the manual's name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

UPPER's layer tones: Temporary Tone (UPPER Layer n) at 11 00 00 00, 11 20 00 00, 11 40 00 00, 11 60 00 00; the synth tone at +01 00 00 in each (Layer 1: common 11 01 00 00, partials 11 01 01 00, 11 01 02 00, 11 01 03 00).

The registration's third tone part is printed "PERC/LOWER" (Registration Part 00 13 00, Sub Part 00 41 00, Sub Modify 00 51 00); its ids are percLower. The Bank Select table (p1) calls it the PERC part.
Live Set Common 2 (10 00 70 00) holds one parameter, MFX Structure (1-5); laid out as upper.liveSet2.

Voice Reserve SOLO and Voice Reserve PERC/LOWER (Registration Common 00 14, 00 15, p19) are printed (0 - 31) with "0 - 31, FULL" beneath: thirty-three labels for thirty-two values (the JUPITER-80 prints 0 - 64 and "0 - 63, FULL"). Kept as the printed 0-31 number, with the line as its description.

Tone Partial FILTER Mode (p23) is printed (0 - 7) with "BYPASS, LPF1, HPF, BPF, PKG" on one line and "LPF2, LPF3, LPF4" on the next, no comma between PKG and LPF2, so the labels count seven for eight values and it stays a number with the line as its description.

The worked example (p25) names its value "SRV REVERB"; the Reverb Type table (p15) has no such entry and lists 02 as SRV ROOM. The bytes are checked as printed: they are the table's address and value.
The transmitted DT1's byte table (p12) gives the device ID as 00H - 1FH, 7FH; the received messages' (p7-8) as 10H - 1FH, 7FH.

Ids follow the parts. Everything of UPPER (its registration Part block, its live set, its layers and their tones) begins upper.; each tone part's registration blocks (Part, Sub Part, Sub Modify, Effect) begin with that part's name; the registration's own blocks with registration.

The offset table names a layer tone's blocks "Synth Tone Common" and "Synth Tone Partial (n)"; the parameter tables laid at them are headed "Tone Common" and "Tone Partial", the only tables of that shape. Laid out as <part>.layer<n>.synthTone and <part>.layer<n>.synthTone.partial<n>.
"Live Set Layer 2" holds only the tone blender's destination settings (Tone Blender Dest Level, Pan, sends, Cutoff …), so it is laid out as <part>.layer<n>.toneBlender.

"Tone Modify Type (read only)" (Live Set Tone Modify, Registration Sub Modify) is printed read only; the generator lays out every ranged row as writable, so it is writable here, and an instrument would presumably ignore the write.

Six rows are printed with a range and no name, and keep the id the generator gives a nameless row: Live Set Common 00 3E and 00 40 (0-1 each, between MFX4 Switch and Reverb Switch and after it), Live Set MFX 00 02 (0-127, after MFX Output Level), Live Set Layer 00 27 (0-127, after Layer Output Level) and 00 2A (0-2, after Layer Output Assign), and Registration Common 00 17 (0-127, after Registration Level). System Common 00 08 is printed with neither a name nor a range and is not laid out.

Two names are misspelt in the manual and keep its spelling: "Control Padal 1 Assign Source" and "Control Padal 2 Assign Source" (System Controller, beside "Control Pedal 1 Assign"), and "FILTER Env Sustatin Level Offset" (Live Set Tone Offset).

The registration's program change is received on the Registration Control Channel (System Common 00 09, 1-16 or OFF), which need not be the channel UPPER plays on; the preset browser sends on the profile's channel, so set that to the registration channel.

Not read at startup (read on request, since the instrument may not answer them): upper.layer1.synthTone, upper.layer1.synthTone.partial1, upper.layer1.synthTone.partial2, upper.layer1.synthTone.partial3, upper.layer2.synthTone, upper.layer2.synthTone.partial1, upper.layer2.synthTone.partial2, upper.layer2.synthTone.partial3, upper.layer3.synthTone, upper.layer3.synthTone.partial1, upper.layer3.synthTone.partial2, upper.layer3.synthTone.partial3, upper.layer4.synthTone, upper.layer4.synthTone.partial1, upper.layer4.synthTone.partial2, upper.layer4.synthTone.partial3.

coverage.inboundControllers: not modelled: what the front panel transmits and what each CC changes are in the Control Change sections (p1-5 received, p9-11 transmitted), not the address map
coverage.registrationController: laid out in two requests: Registration Controller (14 00 30 00, 308 bytes, p19-21) is more than one packet, so it is read as its parameters up to 01 7D and then V-Link Switch at 02 33, skipping 53 reserved bytes
coverage.toneTypes: a layer plays a SuperNATURAL Synth Tone or a SuperNATURAL Acoustic Tone. The address map gives a layer's temporary tone one area, Temporary Synth Tone (+01 00 00), laid out here; an acoustic tone has none, and is edited through the layer's Tone Modify block in the live set (laid out). The manual does not say the synth-tone area answers a request while its layer plays an acoustic tone, and a request it cannot answer gets no reply (p8), so the synth tones are read on request, not at connect
coverage.effectParameterMeanings: type-dependent: MFX and reverb parameters are Roland's 4-nibble container (12768-52768, shown -20000..+20000); what each slot does depends on the selected type, which the MIDI Implementation does not list
coverage.toneModifyMeanings: type-dependent: Modify Parameter 1-32 (a layer's Tone Modify, and the tone parts' Sub Modify) mean what the Tone Modify Type says, and the type is set by the acoustic tone the part plays; the MIDI Implementation does not list the types
coverage.tones: UPPER's four layer tones, all there are: the JUPITER-50 has no LOWER live set. SOLO and PERC/LOWER play one tone each and the address map has no temporary tone area for either: what can be set is their Registration Sub Part and Sub Modify (laid out)
coverage.userData: none in the map: the MIDI Implementation prints only the temporary area, no user registration, live set or tone memory
